definition_evidence: An ordered pair (a,b) has two designated coordinates. A Kuratowski realization is {{a},{a,b}}, so ordered-pair equality holds exactly when both coordinates agree.
mathematical_variant_findings: Wiener and other set-theoretic encodings also satisfy coordinate-uniqueness but are not the same set as Kuratowski's representation
Informal ordered pair as two positions with a first and second coordinate
caution: Do not merge different set-encodings as equal set-theoretic objects. Equivalent coordinate behavior is not identity of representations.

definition_evidence: For sets A and B, A⊆B exactly when every x∈A also belongs to B, without requiring A≠B. Proper subset is a distinct strict concept.
mathematical_variant_findings: Proper subset A⊊B additionally requires A≠B
caution: Keep the non-strict inclusion symbol and do not infer that the entire class of all sets is itself a set in ZFC.
suggested_link_targets: binary relation defined by membership pairs

scope: mapping from X to Y and equivalent total single-valued graph
definition_evidence: For sets X,Y a mapping f:X→Y associates to each x∈X exactly one y∈Y. Equivalently a relation graph G⊆X×Y is total on X and single-valued there; with X,Y fixed this determines a mapping.
mathematical_variant_findings: Typed graph (X,Y,G) with G⊆X×Y and conditions ∀x∈X ∃!y∈Y (x,y)∈G
Bare graph G⊆X×Y when X,Y remain fixed external context; unequal codomain choices can identify the same graph
caution: For the graph-only convention, the subset G does not itself determine a unique codomain Y, including empty-domain cases. Store the function-as-map and typed-graph formulations as context/representation variants and preserve precise equivalence qualifications.
